facts.statement: The holotype of Kosmoceratops was discovered by volunteer Scott Richardson in 2006 and 2007 at localities VP 890 and 951 in the Kaiparowits Formation.
facts.quote: Among the discoveries made were three new ceratopsian (horned dinosaur) taxa, one of which was identified from two localities (UMNH Locality VP 890 and 951) discovered by volunteer field crew member Scott Richardson during the field seasons of 2006 and 2007.

facts.statement: Kosmoceratops richardsoni was named in 2010 by Scott D. Sampson and colleagues, with the holotype specimen being UMNH VP 17000.
facts.quote: In 2010, the paleontologist Scott D. Sampson and colleagues named the new genus and species Kosmoceratops richardsoni, specimen UMNH VP 17000 (from Locality VP 890) being the holotype.

facts.statement: The generic name Kosmoceratops means "ornate horned face" derived from Ancient Greek words for ornamented and horned face.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from the Ancient Greek kosmos, which means "ornamented", and ceratops, which means "horned face".

facts.statement: The specific name richardsoni honors Scott Richardson, who discovered the holotype and many other fossils at the Grand Staircase–Escalante National Monument.
facts.quote: The specific name honors Richardson, who found the holotype and many other fossils at GSENM.

facts.statement: The holotype skull of Kosmoceratops is nearly complete but lacks the predentary bone and parts of the left face and neck frill, and its snout is bent due to postmortem distortion.
facts.quote: The holotype includes a nearly complete adult skull that is missing the predentary bone (the frontmost bone of the lower jaw) and a small part of the left side of the face and neck frill (parts of the jugal, squamosal, and parietal bones), and the snout is bent to the right due to postmortem (after death) distortion.

facts.statement: By 2010, approximately 45 percent of the postcranial skeleton of the holotype was thought to be preserved, with most still under preparation.
facts.quote: 45 percent of the postcranial skeleton was thought to be preserved, most of which was still under preparation by 2010.

facts.statement: In 2020, Denver W. Fowler and Elizabeth A. Freedman Fowler suggested that the assignment of specimen CMN 8801 to Kosmoceratops might be more reliable once better understanding of chasmosaurine skull anatomy is achieved.
facts.quote: In 2020, the paleontologists Denver W. Fowler and Elizabeth A. Freedman Fowler stated that CMN 8801 may be more reliably assigned when better understanding of the anatomy in the front part of chasmosaurine skulls is reached.

facts.statement: Kosmoceratops was estimated to reach a length of 4.5 meters and a weight of 1.2 metric tons.
facts.quote: Kosmoceratops is estimated to have been 4.5 m long and to have weighed 1.2 MT.

facts.statement: Kosmoceratops possessed long main tooth rows forming complex slicing dental batteries with hundreds of teeth behind a toothless beak.
facts.quote: It had long main tooth rows which formed complex slicing dental batteries containing hundreds of teeth behind an edentulous (toothless) beak.

facts.statement: The nasal horncore of Kosmoceratops was unusual among chasmosaurines, being blade-like with an elongated, narrow base and a flattened upper portion.
facts.quote: The nasal horncore (the bony projection from which the nose horn grew) was unusual among chasmosaurines in that it was blade-like, with a base that was elongated and narrow from side to side, and with a flattened upper portion.

facts.statement: The naris of Kosmoceratops was distinct from other ceratopsids, being tall, narrow, distinctly ellipse-shaped, and inclined backward.
facts.quote: The naris (bony nostril opening) was different from other ceratopsids in being tall, relatively narrow from front to back, and distinctly ellipse-shaped (rather than near-circular), with a pronounced hindward inclination.

facts.statement: Unlike most chasmosaurines, Kosmoceratops had supraorbital horncores oriented upward and to the sides, resembling modern bison.
facts.quote: The region around the orbits (eye sockets) was distinctive; while most chasmosaurines had supraorbital horncores (horns above the eyes) that were oriented either forward or hindward, Kosmoceratops and Utahceratops had horncores that were oriented upward and to the sides, superficially similar to those of the modern bison.

facts.statement: Kosmoceratops had a pronounced hump on the skull roof between the orbits, a feature found in few other ceratopsids like Diabloceratops.
facts.quote: Right in front and in the middle of the orbits, the skull roof had a pronounced hump, which was present in few other ceratopsids, such as Diabloceratops.

facts.statement: The neck frill of Kosmoceratops was very derived, sharing several features only with Vagaceratops.
facts.quote: The parietosquamosal neck frill (formed by the parietal and squamosal bones) of Kosmoceratops was very derived (or "advanced"), sharing several features with Vagaceratops only.

facts.statement: Kosmoceratops had a more extreme frill than Vagaceratops, with a width about double its length, smaller and farther-back parietal fenestrae, and more elongated epiossifications.
facts.quote: The frill of Kosmoceratops was more extreme than that of Vagaceratops; its width was about double its length (measured across the surface of the bone), with the parietal fenestrae being much smaller and positioned farther back, and it had more elongated and distinct epiossifications on the hind margin.

facts.statement: An alternate epiossification numbering system was proposed by Fowler and Fowler in 2020, differing from the system used by Sampson and colleagues in 2010.
facts.quote: The epiossification numbering system presented above follows that used by Sampson and colleagues in 2010, but note that Fowler and Fowler proposed an alternate system in 2020, based on comparison with earlier Chasmosaurus species.

facts.statement: In 2010, researchers placed Kosmoceratops in the subfamily Chasmosaurinae based on skull features including a narial strut, a triangular process, and an elongated squamosal bone.
facts.quote: In 2010, Sampson and colleagues placed Kosmoceratops in the latter group due to the premaxilla having a narial strut and a triangular process, as well as the presence of an elongated squamosal bone.

facts.statement: In 2011, Fowler and colleagues hypothesized that Kosmoceratops was an immature growth stage of the species C. irvinensis.
facts.quote: In a 2011 conference abstract, the paleontologist Denver W. Fowler and colleagues suggested that many ceratopsid genera were merely ontogenetic morphs (or growth stages) of other genera and that Kosmoceratops was an immature stage of C. irvinensis

facts.statement: In 2016, Mallon and colleagues found Kosmoceratops and Vagaceratops to form a clade with the genus Spiclypeus as their sister taxon.
facts.quote: In 2016, Mallon and colleagues found Kosmoceratops and Vagaceratops to form a clade, with the new genus Spiclypeus as sister taxon.

facts.statement: Histological studies of Kosmoceratops long bones revealed a dense network of blood vessels and high osteocyte counts, indicating sustained rapid growth.
facts.quote: The bone tissue had a high number of osteocytes (bone cells) as well as a dense network of blood vessels, including radially oriented vascular canals (blood canals running towards the bone interior), indicating sustained rapid growth.

facts.statement: Kosmoceratops bones lacked annual growth lines, unlike northern ceratopsids, suggesting their growth was sustained year-round due to a more equitable southern climate.
facts.quote: The Kosmoceratops and Utahceratops bones sampled by Levitt did not show evidence of lines of arrested growth (annual growth lines), and compared with the ceratopsids Pachyrhinosaurus, Centrosaurus, and Einosaurus from further north which did have growth lines, this may indicate that bone growth reacted to climate

facts.statement: Analysis of bone tissue confirmed that examined Kosmoceratops specimens were subadult to adult, refuting claims that they were immature Vagaceratops.
facts.quote: Levitt determined that the examined Kosmoceratops specimens were subadult to adult, ruling out Fowler and colleagues' 2011 claim that they represented immature Vagaceratops.

facts.statement: Fossilized dung attributed to Kosmoceratops contained angiosperm wood fragments, indicating a diet of woody browse.
facts.quote: The coprolites contained fragments of angiosperm wood (which indicates a diet of woody browse); though there was previously little evidence of dinosaurs consuming angiosperms, these coprolites showed that dinosaurs adapted to feeding on them

facts.statement: Coprolites potentially from Kosmoceratops contained traces of mollusc shells, arthropod cuticle, and lizard bone, suggesting these items were ingested along with plant material.
facts.quote: The coprolites also contained traces of mollusc shell, arthropod cuticle, and lizard bone that may have been ingested along with the plant material.

facts.statement: In 2010, Sampson suggested that the bizarre skull features of Kosmoceratops were likely used for intimidation, fighting rivals, and attracting mates rather than defending against predators.
facts.quote: In a 2010 press release presenting Kosmoceratops, Utahceratops, and Vagaceratops, Sampson stated that most of these "bizarre features" would have been insufficient weapons against predators, but would have been used to intimidate or fight rivals of the same sex and attract individuals of the opposite sex.

facts.statement: In 2013, Hone and Naish criticized the species recognition hypothesis for Kosmoceratops, noting that no living animals use such structures primarily for this purpose.
facts.quote: In 2013, the paleontologists David E. Hone and Darren Naish criticized the "species recognition hypothesis", arguing that no extant animals use such structures primarily for species recognition

facts.statement: Fossils of Kosmoceratops, including an adult skull and partial skeletons, were discovered in the Kaiparowits Formation of the Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument in 2006 and 2007.
facts.quote: Las muestras fueron descubiertas en la formación Kaiparowits del Monumento Nacional Grand Staircase-Escalante en 2006 y 2007, incluyendo un cráneo adulto y esqueleto postcraneal y subadultos parciales.

facts.statement: The adult specimen discovered in the Kaiparowits Formation became the holotype for the new genus and species Kosmoceratops richardsoni in 2010.
facts.quote: En 2010, el adulto se convirtió en el holotipo del nuevo género y especie Kosmoceratops richardsoni.

facts.statement: The specific name richardsoni honors Scott Richardson, who found the specimens.
facts.quote: El nombre específico honra a Scott Richardson, quien encontró los especímenes.

facts.statement: Kosmoceratops had an estimated length of 4.5 meters and a weight of 1.2 tons.
facts.quote: Kosmoceratops tenía una longitud estimada de 4,5 metros y un peso de 1,2 toneladas.

facts.statement: Kosmoceratops had a triangular, pointed beak and a blade-shaped nasal horn with a flattened upper portion.
facts.quote: Tenía un pico triangular con punta puntiaguda y un asta nasal en forma de cuchilla con una porción superior aplanada.

facts.statement: Unlike most relatives whose eye horns pointed forward or backward, Kosmoceratops' eye horns pointed upward and sideways before curving downward to sharp points.
facts.quote: Mientras que los cuernos sobre los ojos estaban orientados hacia adelante o hacia atrás en la mayoría de sus parientes, los cuernos de Kosmoceratops apuntaban hacia arriba y hacia los lados, luego hacia abajo, terminando en puntas puntiagudas.

facts.statement: Kosmoceratops had a short neck frill with small parietal fenestrae, openings through the frill, and ten hook-shaped processes on the posterior margin, eight curving forward and two curving sideways.
facts.quote: El volante del cuello era corto de adelante hacia atrás, con pequeñas fenestras parietales, aberturas a través del volante y diez procesos en forma de gancho en el margen posterior, con ocho curvas hacia adelante y dos curvas hacia los lados.

facts.statement: With fifteen well-developed horns and horn-like structures, Kosmoceratops possessed the most ornamented skull of all known dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Con quince cuernos bien desarrollados y estructuras en forma de cuerno, poseía el cráneo más adornado de todos los dinosaurios conocidos.

facts.statement: Bone histology studies show that Kosmoceratops grew rapidly and had a high metabolism similar to modern birds and mammals.
facts.quote: Los estudios de histología ósea muestran que Kosmoceratops creció rápidamente y tuvo un metabolismo elevado, similar a las aves y mamíferos modernos.

facts.statement: Kosmoceratops lived during the late Cretaceous period, approximately 75 million years ago in the Campanian stage, in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 75 millones de años, en el Campaniense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: The Kaiparowits Formation dates to the late Campanian and was deposited in Laramidia, an island continent, when North America was divided by the Western Interior Seaway.
facts.quote: La formación Kaiparowits data de finales de la era Campaniense y se depositó en Laramidia, un continente insular, cuando Norteamérica fue dividida en el centro por la Vía marítima interior occidental.

facts.statement: The environment where Kosmoceratops lived was dominated by wetlands and supported diverse fauna including the chasmosaurine Utahceratops.
facts.quote: Este ambiente estaba dominado por humedales y sostenía una fauna diversa, incluyendo dinosaurios como el chasmosaurinido Utahceratops.

facts.statement: The genus Kosmoceratops was named by Sampson and colleagues in 2010.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Sampson et al., 2010

facts.statement: The species Kosmoceratops richardsoni was named by Sampson and colleagues in 2010.
facts.quote: species_authority: Sampson et al., 2010

facts.statement: Kosmoceratops is classified as a chasmosaurine ceratopsid.
facts.quote: Kosmoceratops era un ceratópsido chasmosaurinido

facts.statement: It is debated whether Kosmoceratops is closely related to Vagaceratops; some authors suggest Vagaceratops is more closely related to Chasmosaurus.
facts.quote: originalmente se sugirió que estaba estrechamente relacionado con Vagaceratops, que también tenía procesos de curvatura hacia adelante en la parte posterior del volante, pero esto se ha debatido, y algunos autores encontraron que este último estaba más cerca de Chasmosaurus.

facts.statement: The hypothesis that Kosmoceratops in the south was more closely related to the northern geography of Vagaceratops due to provincial divisions in Laramidia has been challenged.
facts.quote: Basado en parte en la relación entre Kosmoceratops y otras chasmosaurinido de la misma época, se ha propuesto que Laramidia se dividió en "provincias" de dinosaurios con zonas endémicas separadas, esta interpretación sugiere que Kosmoceratops en el sur estaba más estrechamente relacionado con la geografía Vagaceratops separados en el norte, pero esto ha sido impugnado.

facts.statement: Kosmoceratops was estimated to be 4.5 meters long and weigh 1.2 tonnes.
facts.quote: Se estima que Kosmoceratops tenía 4,5 metros de largo y pesaba 1,2 toneladas.

facts.statement: As a ceratopsid, Kosmoceratops was likely a quadruped with a strong skeleton, large pelvis, and relatively short tail.
facts.quote: Como ceratópsido, habría sido un cuadrúpedo con un esqueleto muy fuerte, una pelvis grande y una cola relativamente acortada.

facts.statement: Kosmoceratops had long rows of main teeth forming complex cutting batteries containing hundreds of teeth behind a toothless beak.
facts.quote: Tenía largas hileras de dientes principales que formaban complejas baterías de corte que contenían cientos de dientes detrás de un pico, sin dientes.

facts.statement: Kosmoceratops had a triangular upper premaxillary beak with a pointed rostral bone projecting forward and downward.
facts.quote: El pico premaxilar superior de Kosmoceratops era triangular y el hueso rostral más delantero era puntiagudo, con una punta que se proyectaba hacia adelante y hacia abajo.

facts.statement: Kosmoceratops had an unusual blade-shaped nasal projection with a narrow elongated base and flattened upper portion.
facts.quote: La trompa nasal, la proyección ósea de la que creció la trompa nasal, era inusual entre las chasmosaurínidos, ya que tenía forma de cuchilla, con una base alargada y estrecha de lado a lado, y con una porción superior aplanada.

facts.statement: Kosmoceratops had a square-shaped nasal horn positioned relatively far back on the snout.
facts.quote: El cuerno nasal era de forma cuadrangular y estaba colocado relativamente atrás en el hocico.

facts.statement: Kosmoceratops had a high, narrow, elliptical nostril with a pronounced backward inclination, unlike other ceratopsids.
facts.quote: El narina, la abertura de la fosa nasal, era diferente de otros ceratopsidos en ser alto, relativamente estrecho de adelante hacia atrás, y claramente en forma de elipse en lugar de casi circular, con una pronunciada inclinación hacia atrás.

facts.statement: Unlike most chasmosaurines, Kosmoceratops had supraorbital horns oriented upward and sideways, resembling modern bison horns.
facts.quote: Mientras que la mayoría de las chasmosaurinidos tenían cuernos supraorbitales, cuernos sobre los ojos, orientados hacia adelante o hacia atrás, Kosmoceratops y Utahceratops tenían cuernos orientados hacia arriba y hacia los lados, superficialmente similares a los del bisonte moderno.

facts.statement: Kosmoceratops horns were longer and thinner than Utahceratops, curving up and down to sharp points.
facts.quote: En comparación con los cuernos cortos y romos de Utahceratops , los de Kosmoceratops eran más alargados y delgados, curvándose hacia arriba y hacia abajo, terminando en puntas puntiagudas.

facts.statement: Kosmoceratops had a prominent bump on the skull roof between the eyes, a feature also seen in Diabloceratops.
facts.quote: Justo en frente y en el medio de las órbitas, el techo del cráneo tenía una joroba pronunciada, que estaba presente en algunos otros ceratópsidos, como el Diabloceratops.

facts.statement: Kosmoceratops had relatively large epijugal ossifications, known as "cheek horns," typical of chasmosaurines except Chasmosaurus.
facts.quote: Como era típico de los chasmosaurínidos distintos de Chasmosaurus, tenía osificaciones epiyugales relativamente grandes, los "cuernos de mejilla".

facts.statement: Kosmoceratops had high and narrow lateral temporal fenestrae.
facts.quote: Las fenestras temporales laterales, las aberturas a los lados del cráneo, eran altas y estrechas.

facts.statement: Kosmoceratops had a highly derived parietal-squamosal frill sharing features only with Vagaceratops.
facts.quote: El volante del cuello parietal-escamoso, formado por los huesos parietal y escamoso, de Kosmoceratops era muy derivado o "avanzado", compartiendo varias características solo con Vagaceratops.

facts.statement: Kosmoceratops had an extreme frill where width was about double the length, with smaller posterior fenestrae and elongated epiossifications.
facts.quote: El volante de Kosmoceratops fue más extremo que el de Vagaceratops, su ancho era aproximadamente el doble de su longitud, medido a través de la superficie del hueso, con las fenestras parietales siendo mucho más pequeñas y ubicadas más atrás, y tenía epiossificaciones más alargadas y distintas en el margen posterior.

facts.statement: Kosmoceratops had the shortest frill relative to its width among chasmosaurines and the smallest parietal fenestrae relative to total frill area among all ceratopsids.
facts.quote: Aunque las chasmosaurinidos se han considerado tradicionalmente como los ceratópsidos de " volantes largos", Kosmoceratops tenía el volante más corto en relación con su ancho entre las chasmosaurínidos y las fenestras parietales más pequeñas en relación con el área total del volante de cualquier ceratópsidos.

facts.statement: Kosmoceratops had 15 well-developed horns and horn-like structures, making it the most ornamented dinosaur skull known at the time.
facts.quote: Con 15 cuernos bien desarrollados y estructuras en forma de cuerno, por lo tanto Kosmoceratops poseía el cráneo más adornado de todos los dinosaurios conocidos hasta ese momento, esto incluía un núcleo nasal, dos núcleos postorbitales, dos epiyugales y diez epiossificaciones bien desarrolladas en la parte posterior del volante.

facts.statement: Kosmoceratops belongs to the parent group Chasmosaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Chasmosaurinae

facts.statement: Kosmoceratops is classified in the family Ceratopsidae.
facts.quote: Family: Ceratopsidae
